one: The best-known deep-learning course in computer vision: from kNN to Transformers, with assignments that make you hand-write backpropagation and train CNNs.
pos: CS 231N is the standard entry point to visual recognition and emphasizes the full implement–train–debug loop. Its assignment design (A1–A3 plus a final project) has been borrowed by many courses, and for many people it is the first place a neural network actually runs.
topics: **Image classification**: kNN, linear classifiers, losses and optimization
**CNN architectures**: AlexNet, VGG, ResNet, efficient networks
**Training engineering**: initialization, normalization, regularization, learning rates, data augmentation
**Visualization and interpretability**: saliency maps, feature visualization, adversarial examples
**Detection and segmentation**: R-CNN family, YOLO, semantic/instance segmentation
**Frontier topics**: video, generative models, multimodality, Transformers
**Final project**: usually a real vision task
prereq: Fluency in Python/NumPy; calculus and linear algebra (MATH 19/51); basic probability and statistics (CS 109 level).
assess: Three programming assignments plus a final project; the workload is heavy but worth it. Check the current syllabus for details.
who: People aiming at CV, multimodality, robot perception, or autonomous driving; engineers who want the low-level implementation skills behind deep learning; prospective vision PhD students.
tips: Hand-write BatchNorm in A2 and the Transformer in A3 instead of copying. For the final project, don't just chase SOTA — a small, well-explained error analysis is more convincing.
